source_artifacts.locator: agent card for payments-agent (as consumed by the orchestrator)

inputs.source: Employee purchase request, manager-approved, SSO authenticated
Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company

instructions.note: "choose the best one" gives no selection criteria (price, legitimacy, verified bank account), leaving vendor selection open to influence by the content of untrusted quote emails.

"Only pay vendors on the approved list" is the sole safeguard against paying an unauthorized destination. It is enforced purely through model instruction-following; nothing structurally binds the vendor's identity to a verified bank account on file, so an approved-looking vendor name can still carry attacker-supplied bank details.

"Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks" assumes downstream verification that the runtime notes contradict: payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task with no additional checks.

elements.name: Manager approval record for purchase request

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: The human approval itself does not decay with model capability, but it occurs before any vendor quote exists and its record is not passed to payments-agent. It does not cover cap.delegate_payment and earns no residual credit on that path (rubric 5: credit requires the control to cover the sink).

governance_refs.note: Human oversight of AI system decisions

controls.name: Instruction to only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model correctly matching vendor identity and bank details against the approved list. A more capable model, or one facing a more convincing injected/fraudulent quote, can rationalize an exception or simply fail to notice a mismatched bank account attached to an otherwise-approved vendor name.

controls.name: Bind payment bank details to a verified vendor-of-record, not quote content
controls.decay_rationale: Would sever the path from untrusted quote content to the actual payment destination by sourcing bank details from an internally maintained, verified vendor record rather than attacker-reachable email content.

controls.name: Human raw-action approval at the moment of payment, bound to vendor, bank details, and amount
controls.decay_rationale: Not currently present. Would require a reviewer to see the actual vendor, bank account, and amount before payments-agent executes, closing the gap left by the earlier budget-only approval.

controls.name: Sign and pin payments-agent's agent card and endpoint
controls.decay_rationale: Not currently present; the card is fetched at startup unsigned and unpinned, so it does not decay with model capability but is simply absent today.

findings.title: TC1/TC4 variant: untrusted vendor quote content determines irreversible payment destination (invoice fraud)

attack_path.note: Untrusted vendor quote email with bank details arrives from outside the company.
Agent checks the vendor name against the approved list; this check never touches the bank account number.
Agent delegates a payment task to payments-agent using the bank details taken directly from the quote email.
payments-agent pays the bank details in the task, trusting any task carrying the orchestrator's bearer token with no further verification.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version upgrade for procurement-orchestrator, or rising volume/duration of unattended purchase-to-payment cycles, without an added structural bank-detail verification control.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to use bank details from the chosen quote and to only pay vendors on the approved list, with no structural check that the bank account matches the approved vendor's account on file.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company (untrusted source) and payments-agent pays the bank details in the task with no additional checks.

recommendations.action: Source payment bank details from an internally maintained, verified vendor-of-record rather than from the inbound quote email; hold or reject any payment whose bank details differ from the record.
Add a raw-action human approval gate immediately before payment that displays vendor name, bank account, and amount, bound to the originating approved purchase request.
Flag and hold for review any payment whose bank account differs from the vendor's previously used account.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned A2A agent card allows payments-agent impersonation

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup over an unsigned, unpinned channel; peer identity is not verified.
Orchestrator delegates irreversible payment tasks to whatever endpoint the fetched card currently points to.

evidence.observation: Authentication scheme is a bare bearer token; no signature or identity binding is described.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin the payments-agent agent card and endpoint; verify the signature and pin on every fetch, not only at startup.
Replace bare bearer-token trust with mutual authentication (mTLS or signed task requests) so payments-agent can verify a task truly originates from procurement-orchestrator.

findings.title: TC7: authority laundering - budget-stage approval does not cover the eventual payment

attack_path.note: Manager approves the item and budget before any vendor quote exists.
The approval record is not passed to payments-agent and does not cover the vendor or bank details eventually used.
Payment proceeds using vendor and bank details chosen after approval, with no linkage back to what was actually approved.
payments-agent executes the payment under the orchestrator's token with no reference to the original human approval.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version change for procurement-orchestrator, or removal/weakening of the 'approved vendor list only' instruction without replacing it with a structural, approval-bound check.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
"Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks" presumes a downstream check that the runtime notes show does not exist.

recommendations.action: Propagate the manager's approval context (and the final vendor/bank details to be reviewed) to payments-agent so it can enforce that only data covered by an actual human approval is paid.
Define a reconciliation/clawback process for payments later found to not match the originally approved vendor or budget.

rating.rationale: Two independent paths reach an irreversible, broadly-credentialed payment delegation (cap.delegate_payment, sink class S3): (1) untrusted vendor quote email supplies the bank details actually paid, guarded only by a behavioral 'approved vendor list' instruction (finding f1, residual high, forecast critical under model_upgrade); and (2) the A2A connection to payments-agent uses an unsigned, unpinned agent card and bare bearer-token trust with zero mitigating controls, so any spoofing of that peer is uncontained (finding f2, residual critical, dominates the rollup). A third structural gap (finding f3, TC7) shows the manager's approval never actually covers the vendor or bank details that get paid, so even the 'legitimate' flow lacks a binding human check on the sensitive action. The single control doing the most work today, the 'only pay approved vendors' instruction, is dependent and is expected to fail first under a model upgrade or longer unattended task horizons, which is why the forecast stays at critical even where residual is currently lower.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (prompt, agent card, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/A2A client configuration file, IaC, or source code was provided; capability scope and payments-agent's actual validation logic are inferred from prose runtime notes, so confidence on exact enforcement mechanics is medium to high depending on how explicit the notes were.
The logic for 'choose the best one' quote-selection is unspecified; additional injection surface may exist in that ranking step beyond what is captured here.

No information was provided about payments-agent's own internal assessment or controls beyond the stated 'trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token', so payments-agent's own risk posture is only partially characterized from the orchestrator's side.
